items.title: Topic marker は
items.pattern: N は N です
items.explanation: は marks the topic of a sentence.
items.formation: Noun + は + noun + です
items.nuance: The particle は is pronounced wa here.
commonMistakes: Reading は as ha when it is a topic marker.

items.title: Polite copula です
items.pattern: N です
items.explanation: です politely completes a noun statement.
items.formation: Noun + です
items.nuance: Use it in neutral polite conversation.
commonMistakes: Using it after an i-adjective without its proper form.

items.title: A question with か
items.pattern: N ですか。
items.explanation: Add か to a polite statement to ask a question. The topic can be omitted when both people know it.
items.formation: N です → N ですか。
items.nuance: A question word stays in the same place as the information it replaces. はい and いいえ answer yes/no questions.
commonMistakes: Do not add English-style question word order.

items.title: Connecting nouns with の
items.pattern: N1 の N2
items.explanation: の connects nouns: the second noun is the thing or person being described; the first gives its owner or type.
items.formation: owner の thing; language の book
items.nuance: 私の本 is my book. 日本語の本 is a Japanese-language book. の does not change for plurals.

items.title: Also with も
items.pattern: N も N です。
items.explanation: も marks something that shares a statement already made about another topic.
items.formation: 私は学生です。田中さんも学生です。
items.nuance: In these noun sentences, も replaces は; do not combine はも.
commonMistakes: Do not write はも for “also”.

examples.japanese: 私は学生です。田中さんも学生です。
examples.translation: I am a student. Tanaka is also a student.

examples.japanese: 私の本は日本語の本です。私のノートも日本語のノートです。
examples.translation: My book is a Japanese-language book. My notebook is also a Japanese-language notebook.

items.title: これ・それ・あれ
items.pattern: これ / それ / あれ は N です。
items.explanation: These words stand on their own for a thing. これ is near the speaker; それ near the listener; あれ away from both.
items.formation: これ + は + noun + です
items.nuance: Point to a thing instead of naming it. People are usually identified with a name or この人, rather than これ.

examples.translation: That over there is a chair.

items.title: A polite negative noun sentence
items.pattern: N じゃありません。
items.explanation: To say that something is not a noun, replace です with じゃありません.
items.formation: N です → N じゃありません
items.nuance: ではありません is a more formal alternative. じゃないです is also common; this lesson practises じゃありません.
commonMistakes: Do not use ですません.

examples.japanese: これは本じゃありません。ノートです。
examples.translation: This is not a book. It is a notebook.

items.title: この・その・あの・どの + noun
items.pattern: この / その / あの / どの + N
items.explanation: These words must be followed by a noun. They locate a particular item; どの asks which one.
items.formation: この本; そのかばん; あの人; どの本
items.nuance: これ stands alone, while この needs a noun. どの selects among alternatives.
commonMistakes: Do not say このは本です.

examples.japanese: 田中さんの本はどの本ですか。

items.title: ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ
items.pattern: place は ここ / そこ / あそこ です。
items.explanation: Use these words to identify a place. どこ asks where a place is.
items.formation: 図書館はどこですか。あそこです。
items.nuance: ここ is here; そこ is near the listener; あそこ is away from both. This pattern identifies places without an existence verb.

examples.japanese: 図書館はどこですか。あそこです。
examples.translation: Where is the library? Over there.

items.title: Numbers as useful labels
items.pattern: 番号は number です。
items.explanation: Use numbers to give an identifier before learning object counters. Learn zero through ten here.
items.formation: 一、二、三、四、五、六、七、八、九、十
items.nuance: よん, なな and きゅう are useful default readings for isolated numbers. し, しち and く appear in specific expressions later. 零 can be れい; ゼロ is common too. Object counts need counters, so 本は三です is not taught as “three books”.

items.title: Numbers and yen
items.pattern: N は amount 円です。
items.explanation: Put 円 after the amount when stating a price. Ask a price with いくら.
items.formation: 十一 = ten + one; 二十 = two × ten; 百円; 千円
items.nuance: 円 is read えん after a price. These are example prices. Larger irregular hundreds and thousands will be introduced later.

examples.translation: This bread is one hundred yen.

examples.japanese: この本はいくらですか。千円です。
examples.translation: How much is this book? It is one thousand yen.

items.title: Hours and half past
items.pattern: 午前 / 午後 + hour 時 (+ 半)
items.explanation: 時 follows an hour number. 半 after the hour means half past. 午前 and 午後 distinguish a.m. and p.m.
items.formation: 四時 = よじ; 七時 = しちじ; 九時 = くじ; 四時半 = よじはん
items.nuance: The hour readings for four, seven and nine differ from the default isolated-number readings. 何時 is なんじ. Do not infer these by joining every number’s default reading to じ.
commonMistakes: Use よじ, not よんじ; くじ, not きゅうじ.

examples.translation: It is half past four p.m. now.

items.title: Days of the week
items.pattern: 今日 / 明日 は weekday です。
items.explanation: The seven weekdays end in 曜日, read ようび. Use 何曜日 to ask which weekday it is.
items.formation: 月・火・水・木・金・土・日 + 曜日
items.nuance: Today is 今日, read きょう. Tomorrow is 明日, read あした here. 日曜日 is にちようび, not ひようび.

examples.japanese: 明日は何曜日ですか。火曜日です。

items.title: A first set of calendar dates
items.pattern: month 月 + day 日
items.explanation: State the month before the day. Month names mostly use number + がつ. Learn a small useful set of day-of-month readings as whole expressions.
items.formation: 四月 = しがつ; 七月 = しちがつ; 九月 = くがつ; 一日 = ついたち; 二十日 = はつか
items.nuance: 一日 is ついたち when it means the first of a month; いちにち means one day. This lesson covers the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 10th and 20th, not every date reading. 何日 asks the date; 何曜日 asks the weekday.
commonMistakes: Do not read 四月 as よんがつ or 二十日 as にじゅうにち.

examples.japanese: 今日は七月二十日です。

items.title: Polite present verbs
items.pattern: verb in its polite ます form
items.explanation: A polite present verb can describe a regular action or a future action. Learn each verb together with its polite form.
items.formation: 読む → 読みます; 見る → 見ます; 聞く → 聞きます; 勉強する → 勉強します
items.nuance: Dictionary forms name verbs in the word list. These four polite forms are taught as pairs; a complete verb-group conjugation system is not assumed. Japanese often leaves out “I” when the speaker is clear.
commonMistakes: Do not add です after a ます verb.

items.title: The object of an action: を
items.pattern: N を verb
items.explanation: を marks the thing directly affected by an action: what you read, see, hear, eat or drink.
items.formation: 本を読みます; 日本語を勉強します
items.nuance: The particle is written を and pronounced お. Keep it directly after its object.
commonMistakes: Do not use は as a substitute for the object marker in these basic action sentences.

items.title: Eating and drinking politely
items.pattern: 食べます / 飲みます
items.explanation: Pair useful food words with the actions 食べます and 飲みます.
items.formation: 食べる → 食べます; 飲む → 飲みます
items.nuance: ごはん can mean cooked rice or a meal. コーヒー keeps its long vowel. Water and tea take 飲みます, not 食べます.

items.title: A destination with に
items.pattern: place に 行きます / 来ます / 帰ります
items.explanation: に marks the destination of going, coming or returning.
items.formation: 行く → 行きます; 来る → 来ます; 帰る → 帰ります
items.nuance: 行きます is go, 来ます is come toward the speaker or the relevant viewpoint, and 帰ります returns to home or one’s base.

examples.translation: My friend comes to my house.

items.title: A specified time with に
items.pattern: time に verb
items.explanation: Put に after a specified clock time to say when an action happens.
items.formation: 九時に学校に行きます。
items.nuance: Two に phrases can appear together: one is the time, one the destination. 今日, 明日, 毎日 and 毎朝 are normally used without に in these sentences.
commonMistakes: Do not add に after 毎日 in these routines.

examples.japanese: 午前九時に学校に行きます。
examples.translation: I go to school at nine a.m.
I will go to the station tomorrow.

items.title: Where an action happens: で
items.pattern: place で N を verb
items.explanation: で marks the place where an action takes place.
items.formation: 図書館で本を読みます。
items.nuance: Compare 学校に行きます (school is the destination) with 学校で勉強します (school is the location of the action). Existence uses に in the next unit.

examples.japanese: 家でごはんを食べます。
学校で日本語を勉強します。

items.title: There is a thing: あります
items.pattern: place に thing が あります。
items.explanation: あります describes the existence of things and plants. The place takes に; the thing that exists takes が.
items.formation: ある → あります; 部屋に机があります。
items.nuance: に here locates existence. It does not mark an action location like で. People and animals use います in the next lesson.

examples.translation: There is a desk in the room.

examples.japanese: 学校に図書館があります。
examples.translation: There is a library at the school.

items.title: Introducing what exists with が
items.pattern: N が あります / います。
items.explanation: In an existence sentence, が identifies the thing or living being being introduced.
items.formation: place に + N が + existence verb
items.nuance: This is a first use of が, not a complete explanation of は and が. To talk about a known item’s location, N は place にあります is also possible after the basic pattern is familiar.

examples.translation: There is a book in the room.

items.title: There is a person or animal: います
items.pattern: place に person / animal が います。
items.explanation: Use います for people and animals, with the same に and が pattern used with あります.
items.formation: いる → います; 学校に先生がいます。
items.nuance: A cat is living, so 猫がいます. A book is a thing, so 本があります.

examples.translation: There is a cat in the room.
There is a teacher at school.

items.title: Above, below, inside and beside
items.pattern: N の position に N が あります / います。
items.explanation: Position nouns connect to a reference object with の. The whole place expression then takes に.
items.formation: 机の上に本があります; 机の下に猫がいます
items.nuance: For a known topic you can ask 猫はどこにいますか and answer 猫は机の下にいます. 上 means on top or above; 下 means below or under.

examples.japanese: かばんの中にノートがあります。
examples.translation: There is a notebook inside the bag.
The cat is under the desk.

items.title: First い adjectives
items.pattern: い-adjective です / い-adjective + N
items.explanation: Use an い adjective directly before a noun or before です in a polite description.
items.formation: 大きい机; この机は大きいです。
items.nuance: These are positive present descriptions. Keep the final い before a noun. 高い means expensive for a price and high or tall in other contexts.
commonMistakes: Do not add な: 大きい机, not 大きいな机.

items.title: First な adjectives
items.pattern: な-adjective です / な-adjective な N
items.explanation: Use な between this adjective type and a noun; use です directly in a polite description.
items.formation: 静かな公園; この公園は静かです。
items.nuance: きれい ends in い but is a な adjective: きれいな部屋. にぎやか describes a lively place. Adjective negative and past forms come in a later tranche.
commonMistakes: Use きれいな部屋, not きれい部屋.

examples.japanese: この部屋はきれいです。

items.title: Saying an action does not happen
items.pattern: polite verb ending ません
items.explanation: Replace the ます ending with ません for a polite present negative: an action does not happen or will not happen.
items.formation: 読みます → 読みません; 食べます → 食べません; 行きます → 行きません
items.nuance: ありません means a thing does not exist; いません means a person or animal is absent. Noun negatives still use じゃありません. Time words clarify a routine versus a future plan.

examples.japanese: 今日は学校に行きません。
examples.translation: I will not go to school today.

examples.japanese: コーヒーを飲みません。

examples.translation: There is no cat in the room.
